title: 2D side-scrolling platformer
summary: Gravity, jumping, solid tiles you stand on, hazards you do not. Side-on camera that follows the player horizontally.

layers.name: Paralax
layers.doc: Distant background, scrolls slower than the world. Spelled with one L to match the engine's alias table in scripts/core/depth.py.

layers.name: Floor
layers.doc: The ground the player stands on -- and the layer passability is authored against. A tile here is ART, not a solid: the engine reads solidity from this layer's COMPANION layer (FloorCollision by default, or whatever this layer's pyoneer_passability property names), which the editor's collision mode creates on the first mask stroke. A tile with no mask painted over it blocks nothing.

layers.name: GroundClutter
layers.doc: Non-solid decoration behind the player: signs, pipes, background bricks.

layers.name: PlayerDepth
layers.doc: Tiles that interleave with the player.

layers.name: Above1
layers.doc: Above the player, below the foreground.

layers.name: Foreground
layers.doc: Draws over everything: foliage, girders, foreground scenery the player passes behind.

layers.name: entity
layers.doc: Spawn points, enemies, pickups, hazards and triggers. An object's Type names a class in scripts/core/spawn.py's SPAWN_REGISTRY and resolves to a depth through OBJECT_CONVERTER; a Type that is not registered makes the map RAISE at load, which is why this list is exactly the registry and not a wish list. What the object DOES is its pyoneer_behaviors property -- see docs/BEHAVIORS.md -- so a side-on player and a top-down one are the same GamePlayer with different lists.

tables.name: actors
tables.title: Actors
tables.doc: The player and every enemy. Movement numbers live here, not in Python. These column names are also the parameter keys a behavior declares with source="actors" -- a behavior that wants gravity asks for the column called gravity, and docs/BEHAVIORS.md lists which behavior consumes which column.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: Shown to the player.

fields.name: animation
fields.doc: Key into config/animations.json.

fields.name: hp
fields.doc: Hit points.

fields.name: move_speed
fields.doc: Horizontal pixels per second at full run.

fields.name: jump_velocity
fields.doc: Upward pixels per second at the instant of jump. Negative is up in screen space; store it positive and negate at use.

fields.name: gravity
fields.doc: Downward pixels per second squared. Per-actor so a floaty boss is data, not a special case.

fields.name: max_fall_speed
fields.doc: Terminal velocity, so nothing tunnels through a floor.

fields.name: air_control
fields.doc: Fraction of ground SPEED usable mid-air, 0 to 1. platformer_move multiplies horizontal speed by this while airborne; it is not an acceleration term.

fields.name: coyote_ms
fields.doc: Milliseconds after leaving a ledge during which a jump still counts. Set 0 for strict.

fields.name: contact_damage
fields.doc: Damage dealt to whatever it touches. 0 for the player.

fields.name: playable
fields.doc: Authoring metadata only -- NOTHING reads this at runtime. What actually decides who the human drives is the player_input token in the object's pyoneer_behaviors list; see docs/BEHAVIORS.md. Kept as a designer-facing filter, not as a switch.

tables.name: weapons
tables.title: Weapons
tables.doc: Guns and anything else that emits a projectile.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: Shown to the player.

fields.name: damage
fields.doc: Hit points removed per projectile.

fields.name: fire_interval_ms
fields.doc: Milliseconds between shots. Lower is faster.

fields.name: projectile_speed
fields.doc: Pixels per second.

fields.name: projectile_life_ms
fields.doc: Milliseconds before the projectile despawns.

fields.name: spread_degrees
fields.doc: Random cone half-angle. 0 is perfectly accurate.

fields.name: ammo_capacity
fields.doc: Shots per magazine. 0 means unlimited.

fields.name: automatic
fields.doc: Does holding the button keep firing?

tables.name: levels
tables.title: Levels
tables.doc: Play order and per-level rules. One row per map.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: Shown on the level select.

fields.name: map
fields.doc: A map name from config/maps.json.

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Play order, ascending.

fields.name: par_seconds
fields.doc: Target completion time for scoring. 0 disables.

fields.name: music
fields.doc: Audio key.
